column1: # pins.tsv — the single statement of which tool versions this repo expects.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS.
# The pins were spread across four places: MODULE.bazel (shellcheck, buildifier,
# via rules_python norminette), tools/requirements.txt, .devcontainer/Dockerfile
# (the apt toolchain) and .bazelrc (which compiler Bazel drives). Nothing stated
# them together, so nothing could check them, and "does this box still match the
# campus?" had no answer short of reading four files by hand.
# tools/env_drift.sh reads this and compares it against whatever the current
# machine actually has. Run on a campus box, it is the whole answer to "have they
# upgraded anything?".
# THREE KINDS OF PIN, and the difference matters.
#   fetched  Bazel downloads it against a sha256 and every layer runs THAT
#            binary, so THIS MACHINE'S copy is not consulted at all -- an apt
#            shellcheck 0.8.0 sitting beside our pinned 0.10.0 is not drift, it
#            is irrelevant. The comparison that means something for these is
#            pin-against-fetch, which is the `fetched-as` column below.
#   campus   The version must MATCH THE CAMPUS BOX, because the Moulinette
#            compiles and runs with it. A mismatch means the suite is testing
#            something other than what the grade comes from -- the failure this
#            whole exercise exists to prevent. These are the ones to re-pin when
#            campus moves.
#   ours     Our own tooling. Nobody's grade depends on it; the only requirement
#            is that everyone gets the SAME one, so it drifts only when we choose
#            to move it. A campus upgrade is irrelevant to these.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   tool  kind  expected-substring  version-command  pinned-in
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   tool  kind  expected-full-line  version-command  pinned-in  [fetched-as]
# expected-full-line is the WHOLE first line the version command printed on the
# machine this was pinned from, suffix and all. It used to be a substring --
# `clang version 12.` -- so that Ubuntu could repackage without reporting drift.
# Right instinct, wrong mechanism: "do not fail on packaging noise" became
# "cannot see the difference at all", and a campus move from 12.0.1 to 12.0.5
# would have gone unnoticed. env_drift.sh now records the full line and GRADES
# the difference instead: major is loud, minor/patch says re-audit, and a
# changed packaging suffix alone is noted and forgiven. Nothing is thrown away.
# fetched-as is optional and names an environment variable holding the path to
# the binary BAZEL DOWNLOADED for this tool, set by //tools:env_drift in
# tools/BUILD.bazel. Where it is present, env_drift compares three things rather
# than two -- the pin, the box, and the fetch -- because once a layer stops
# using the box's binary, "the pin matches the box" no longer implies "the pin
# matches what our checks actually run".
# A VERSION-COMMAND OF `-` means "recorded here, deliberately not probed".
# Two rows need it -- bazel and bazelisk -- for one reason: asking either its
# version from inside `bazel run //tools:env_drift` re-enters Bazel and
# contends for the lock that very command is holding. They are still checked,
# just not from here: //tools:conventions verifies that the version this file
# records is the version .bazelversion, tools/setup.sh and the Dockerfile
# actually install, which is the drift that can realistically happen to them.
# ONE ROW IS OBSERVED BUT NOT PINNED: glibc.
# It is here because it is the only entry that is not a tool but the RUNTIME
# every deliverable links against, and because nothing was watching it at all.
# It is not fetched, and pinning it would mean shipping a SYSROOT -- headers, the
# shared objects, the crt files and a linker configured to prefer them -- which
# is a different order of work from pointing a runner at a fetched driver.
# The reason that is an acceptable trade, rather than a hole: the allowed-
# function lists across the whole Piscine come to eight libc symbols (write,
# malloc, free, read, open, close, strerror, basename), all POSIX, none of whose
# behaviour has moved in decades. Exactly one of them can produce an observable
# a libc version could change -- strerror's message text, asserted byte for byte
# in c-piscine-c-10/tests/ex01/errmsg.txt -- and the locale that decides that
# text is already fixed for every test in .bazelrc. Linking is forward-
# compatible, and unlike the compiler (whose campus copy differs from the
# student's) the harness builds and runs on the same machine, so there is no
# skew to protect against.
# The value expected here was observed in the DEVCONTAINER, not on campus: the
# 2026-08-09 campus audit predates env-audit.sh capturing glibc at all. Ubuntu
# 22.04.5 ships 2.35, so it should match; the next campus run is what confirms
# it, and the packaging suffix will differ harmlessly (env_drift grades that as
# "repackaged").
# WHEN CAMPUS MOVES: run `bazel run //tools:env_drift` there, read what it
# reports, and edit BOTH this file and the place named in `pinned-in`. Repinning
# is deliberately manual -- a pin changed automatically is a change to what the
# suite tests, made by nobody.
cc
